transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I... well, I was told I should come in. It’s mostly about... my father’s death. 

Look, everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up perfectly. But... I work with systems. I look at the data. When I actually compare the timestamps, the missing attachments... and just the way certain community members avoid my questions when I bring it up... it’s obvious to me. Someone is hiding what really happened to him. 

I just... I don't really want to get into a whole debate about it, but the discrepancies are right there.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
No. I... no. I don't hear voices or anything like that.
How long have you been convinced that there were discrepancies regarding your father's death?
About nine months. It was... just after he passed away. I had to sort through his records and, you know, his messages. That's when I started looking at it.
Do you feel that these community members are actively trying to harm you or sabotage your life because you've discovered the truth about your father?
No. I... I never said that. I don't think anyone is trying to hurt me. They just... they just avoid the topic. That's all I've noticed.
Are there any other situations or areas of your life where you feel you have uncovered a truth that others are ignoring or covering up?
No. Just... just the stuff with my dad. I don't go looking for things like that.
Have you ever considered that there might be a simpler explanation for the missing attachments or the way people avoid the subject?

I... I know what people say. Everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up. But... I look at the timestamps. The missing attachments. And then the way certain community members just avoid my questions when I bring it up... it's just obvious to me. Someone is hiding what really happened around his death. I don't see a simpler explanation.
Has this preoccupation with your father's death caused you to miss work, withdraw from friends, or neglect your daily responsibilities?

No. I... I still go to work. I handle my projects, pay my bills... keep my normal routine. Everything gets done. The only time there's any... tension, I guess... is just when I bring up my questions about the records with my family or people in the community. But no, I haven't neglected anything.
